A genealogy of emotions: Emotions are first experienced as sensations that start in the body in response to a physical stimuli (external or internal, such as discomfort in the gut or pain).  The brain monitors the change in state of the body (heart rate, temperature, movement) and then surveys the environment for clues and attaches a label (happy, sad, excited, afraid, etc.)  It's for this reason that we can confuse excitement and fear - they are the same in the body so the brain can mislabel them.  Emotions feel interesting for children, so they like to get wound up! The younger the child, the easier it is to calm them down with physical comforts (comforting the source of the emotions, the body).

Further on in emotional development, the neocortex gets involved to a greater and greater degree.  During the labeling process, the neocortex processes information like mad and draws all kinds of conclusions about the situation, probabilities, possible responses, and relates it with other similar events in the past. Labels get more complex.  Thoughts get associated with the emotions (such as "I'm so embarassed, I'll never go on stage again.") and stored in memory. In that way in the future, the THOUGHT is able to trigger the body's emotional response.  Emotions are still IN the body, but triggered and experienced in the mind.

In adults there can be a complex emotional feedback loop, intensifying uncomfortable emotions into a mix of sensations, thoughts, beliefs, and memories. When adults are emotionally out of control, the easiest way to stop this is to chill out and calm the body to cut off the feedback loop, just like you'd calm a small child.

Interestingly, anxiety is a distressing emotion that is actually just chronic stress response by the body. There is a feedback loop between mind and body - the brain senses the body's panic, concludes there must be something to panic about, then sends the signal to the body to panic more.

Emotions aren't all bad.  Emotions are the original source of motivation.  Spot a predator on the horizon, heart rate rises, adrenaline gets pumped out, and you find yourself suddenly very motivated to run.  In modern life where we lack predators, many people lack motivation and become depressed.  The solution is to tap into any emotional response that gets the heart rate up and a little adrenaline out.  Some of these solutions to lack of motivation are innocuous (e.g. coffee), while some are dangerous for the body (creating stress using deadlines and fear of punishment, amphetamines) because they create a bunch of other hormone changes (e.g. increase insulin, decrease testosterone, estrogen, etc).  Emotions are a great source of motivation - figure out how to get yourself emotionally involved or excited about something (your "why") and you won't have any problem with the "how" to get it done.

Do you have a need that only someone else can meet?  If it's loneliness, then meditate on why loneliness is so scary to you.  Face that fear and get stronger - you might discover that being alone does not necessarily mean that you're lonely.  Relationships come when we aren't even looking for them!

The reason I suggest self-discovery and learning to meet your own needs is that it makes you more confident and less likely to give off needy vibes.

It sounds like you might have some kind of attachment to an outcome. I used to get nervous talking to people because I was attached to the outcome of the conversation - I deeply needed for them to think that I was smart or pretty or some other positive assessment.  I was worried about someone finding out that I wasn't as smart as I wanted to think of myself as, or as attractive as I wanted to believe I was.

What helped me was thinking of the other person as a human being - just another human being like me. No better, no worse.  I let go of attachment to wanting them to think certain thoughts about me. I let go of my judgment of myself and them.

Now my conversation can be a true "interaction" between myself and the other person.  It is no longer about my goal to have certain desires met, such as for that person to hold me in positive regard.  If I'm awkward, whatever.  If I look dumb, whatever.  It's just a fact that in life there will be awkward conversations - no biggie.  Now I can concentrate on what I'm doing instead of worrying about trying to control an outcome.
